title: THE LAND
blurb: Mountains, rocks, fields, hillsides and ice.

radicals.name: MOUNTAIN
radicals.origin: Three peaks in a row, the tallest in the middle. It has hardly changed in three thousand years.
ex: a bird 鸟 resting on a mountain in the sea
where the land rises out of the water
the very top of a mountain
radicals.watch: 山 moves around: on the left in 峰, on top in 岸, underneath in 岛. Wherever it sits, think high ground. 出 (to go out) looks like two mountains stacked up, but it is not one of the family.

radicals.name: STONE
radicals.origin: A rock 口 lying at the foot of a cliff 厂. The everyday word for a stone is 石头.
ex: the first bowls were carved from stone
radicals.watch: Look-alike: 右 (right) has the same box, but its top stroke crosses the long one. In 石 the top stroke stops where they meet.

radicals.name: FIELD
radicals.origin: Farmland seen from above: four plots with raised paths between them.
radicals.clue: farmland and what it is used for
ex: strength 力 at work in the field
the lines between one field and the next
at first it meant marking out the edges of a field
radicals.watch: 田 is a common building block where it is not the radical: 思 (to think) is filed under heart and 累 (tired) under silk. Look-alikes with a stroke poking out: 由, 甲 and 申.

radicals.name: HILL
radicals.origin: 阜 is a mound, drawn as steps cut into a hillside. As a radical it shrinks to a hook that looks like an ear, always on the LEFT of the character.
radicals.clue: hills, slopes and walls of earth
ex: ground closed in by earth walls
the sunny side of the hill
the shady side of the hill
a steep slope is a risky place
radicals.watch: The same ear on the RIGHT is a different radical: town, as in 都 (capital) and 邮 (post). Left ear means hill. Right ear means town.

radicals.name: ICE
radicals.origin: Two cracks in a frozen pond. Think of it as water with one drop frozen away: 氵 has three dots, 冫 has two.
ex: ice 冫 beside water 水
radicals.watch: Count the dots. Three is water (江, river). Two is ice (冷, cold). A few everyday characters carry 冫 with no cold in them at all: 决 (to decide) and 况 (situation).
